title: Variable Extraction for Model Recovery in Scientific Literature

model.params_source: assumed (temperature not found in the extracted text; the triage note records 0); judge output limited to one token (Sec. 'GPT-4 as a Similarity Evaluator')

task.approximation: pure setup: the Figure 4 template without the few-shot and tool-extraction segments; pairwise similarity judged by the same live snapshot; the pair text handed to the judge is 'name | description' / 'name | value' (format not printed); F1 pooled over chunks (Table 1 says 'average performance'; per-chunk averages are printed as the alternative)

items.license: unknown (no license file in the repository)

fields_paper.label: annotation records per chunk with type (variable description / variable value), highlighted text and span (key names unverified)

prompt.user_template:
Please extract variable names and descriptions from the following paper text.
Here is some paper text:
{text}
This text may contain model related variables or parameters, their initial values and what they mean. If it does, list each of the variables on a separate line with the following attributes separated by "|":
name | description | numerical value.
If the variable's value uses other variables or there is no value for the variable, output "None" for that variable value; do not hallucinate a variable value or variable description that does not exist in the text.
prompt.few_shot: none (the 3-shot variant is a different Table 1 row)
prompt.source_location: Figure 4 (prompt templates for variable extraction; black-font standard template)
prompt.verbatim: partial (the sentence 'You may refer to the provided tool extractions for your reference.' and the [TOOL EXTRACTION] paragraph belong to the tool-enhanced variant and are omitted; [OPTIONAL EXAMPLES] omitted for the pure setup)

output.postprocess: build prediction entries of type 'var desc' (name + description) and 'var val' (name + value, value != None); for each chunk form the Cartesian product of predictions and gold entries of the same type and ask the judge 'y'/'n'
output.parse_paper: regex per line ^(.+?)\s*\|\s*(.+?)\s*\|\s*(.+?)$ -> (name, description, value); value 'None' means no value entry

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: recall = share of gold entries with at least one judged match, precision = share of predicted entries with at least one judged match, F1 = harmonic mean (Sec. 'Evaluation Metrics'), pooled over all chunks

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare 2026-09-07: est_usd_prepare counts <=400 output tokens per free-text call (runner out_guess); est_usd_dryrun_max_tokens counts the full max_tokens

notes: 556 extraction calls (~$0.02) plus roughly 30K judge pairs at one output token (~$0.002 each).
